en.title: Fateha Khwani
en.intro: Fateha Khwani is a traditional gathering in which du'a (supplication) is made, and the reward (thawab) of reciting the Qur'an, dhikr, or other acts of worship is dedicated to the deceased, with the hope that Allah grants them its benefit.

sections.title: START
sections.text:
Bismillaahir Rahmaanir Raheem::
|||
Surah Al-Ahzab (Surah No. 33 : Verse 56)::1. Indeed, Allah and (all) His angels (continuously) invoke blessings upon the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him). O believers! You, too, invoke blessings upon him and salute him with worthy salutations of peace.
|||
Darood Sharif::O Allah, send Your blessings upon our Master and Patron Muhammad, and upon the family of our Master and Patron Muhammad, and bestow Your blessings and grant peace.
|||
Awraade Wazaaif::
|||
Surah An-Nahl (Surah No. 16 : Verse 98)::1. So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
|||
Surah Al-Mumeenoon (Surah No. 23 : Verses 97-98)::2. And say: ‘My Lord! I seek refuge in You from the evil incitements of the devils.
3. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they should be present with me.’
|||
Surah An-Nas (Surah No. 114 : Verses 4-6)::3. from the evil of the whisperings of the sneaky (Satan),
4. who whispers into the breasts of humans,
5. from among the jinn and humans.’
|||
Bismillaahir Rahmaanir Raheem::
|||
::1. Bismillahil Khaalikil Akbarihil Zammimma Wa Khauf O Was Salaam
2. Wa'Ala Kudratilil Makhlooke Ma'al Khaalike
|||
Surah Maryam (Surah No. 19 : Verse 1)::3. Kaf, Ha, Ya, ‘Ayn, Sad.
|||
Surah Ash-Shura (Surah No. 42 : Verses 1-2)::4. Ha-Mim,
5. ‘Ayn, Sin, Qaf.
|||
Surah Ta-Ha (Surah No. 20 : Verse 111)::6. All faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the All-Sustaining. And surely, he who bears (the burden of) injustice will certainly fail.
|||
Surah Al-Imran (Surah No. 3 : Verse 173 last part)::7. and Allah is Sufficient for us, and He is an excellent Guardian!

sections.title: SAWAAB-E-TAKBIR
sections.text: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. And Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. (3 TIME)

sections.title: START EACH SURAH WITH BISMILLAH AND END IT WITH DAROOD SHARIF
Surah Al-Fateha (Surah No. 1)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. All praise be to Allah, the Lord of all worlds,
2. the Most Compassionate, the All-Merciful,
3. Master of the Day of Judgement.
4. (O Allah!) You alone we worship, and from You alone we seek help.
5. Guide us upon the straight path,
6. the path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray.

sections.title: Ya Ya Sin
sections.text:
1. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah.
2. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O Prophet of Allah.
3. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O Beloved of Allah.
4. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O Beloved of Allah.
5. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O one granted intercession by Allah.
6. O Ya Sin, may Allah send blessings upon you, O Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

sections.title: Surah Ya Sin (Surah No. 36)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Ya-Sin.
2. By the Wise Qur’an,
3. you are indeed one of the messengers,
4. upon the straight path.
5. (This is a revelation) sent down gradually from the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful,
6. so that you may warn a people whose ancestors were not warned, so they are heedless.
7. The Word has already proved true against most of them, but they do not believe.
8. We have put iron shackles around their necks, which (reach) up to (their) chins. So their heads are turned up.
9. We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and then We have veiled them so they do not see.
10. It is the same for them: whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.
11. You (can) only warn the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most-Compassionate (Lord) without seeing Him. So give him the glad tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward.
12. Indeed, it is We Who revive the dead and write down what they have sent forth and their effects (which they have left behind). We have counted everything in a clear Record.
13. And set out for them an example of the people of a town when the messengers came to them.
14. When (at first) We sent them two (messengers), they rejected both of them, then We reinforced (the two) with the third, and they declared: ‘We (all) have been sent to you (as messengers).’
15. They said: ‘You are only human beings like us, and the Most- Compassionate (Lord) has not revealed anything. You are just lying.’
16. They (the messengers) said: ‘Our Lord knows that we have been sent to you.
17. And we are not responsible except for clear communication (of the message).’
18. They answered: ‘We take you as an evil fortune. If you do not stop, we shall certainly stone you, and surely a painful punishment will afflict you from us.’
19. They (the messengers) said: ‘Your evil fortune lies within yourselves. (Why do you take it as an evil omen) when you are reminded (of the truth)? Instead, you are a transgressing people.’
20. And a person came running from the farthest end of the city. He said: ‘O my people, follow the messengers.
21. Follow those who do not ask you for any reward, and they are rightly guided.
22. Why should I not worship Him Who has originated me, and to Whom you shall be returned?
23. Should I take gods besides Him? If the Most-Compassionate (Lord) intends to cause me any harm, their intercession will not benefit me in any way, nor will they be able to rescue me.
24. Indeed, I would then be in a clear error.
25. I do believe in your Lord, so listen to me (attentively).’
26. (The disbelievers killed him, then) it was said (to him): ‘Enter Paradise!’ He said: ‘Alas! If only my people could know,
27. for what my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honoured ones.’

sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
|||
Sura Ya Sin (Sura No. 36 : Verse 58)[5 Times]::1. ‘Peace!’ (It will be) a word (of greeting) from the All-Merciful Lord.
|||
Sura As-Saffat (Sura No. 37 : Verse 79)::2. ‘Peace be upon Nuh (Noah) throughout the nations!’
|||
Sura As-Saffat (Sura No. 37 : Verse 109)::3. Peace be upon Ibrahim (Abraham)!
|||
Sura As-Saffat (Sura No. 37 : Verse 120)::4. Peace be upon Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron)!
|||
Sura As-Saffat (Sura No. 37 : Verse 130)::5. Peace be upon Ilyas (Elias)!
|||
Sura Az-Saffat (Sura No. 37 : Verse 181)::6. Peace be upon the messengers!
|||
Sura Al-Zumar (Sura No. 39 : Verse 73)[Last Part]::7. Peace be upon you! You are welcome! Enter it to remain here forever.
|||
Sura Al-Qadr (Sura No. 39 : Verse 73)::8. It is (all) peace until the rising of the dawn.

sections.title: Ayat al-Kursi (Surah No. 2 : Verse 255)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Allah! There is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the All-Sustainer. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them. They cannot comprehend anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, and it does not tire Him to preserve them both. He is the All-Exalted, the All-Supreme.

sections.title: Amanar Rasul (Surah No. 2 : Verses 285-286)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. The Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. They all believe in Allah, His angels, His Books and His Messengers. (They declare:) ‘We make no distinction between any of His Messengers.’ And they say: ‘We hear and obey. (Grant us) Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.’
2. Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. Whatever (good) it earns will be for its (own) benefit, and whatever (evil) it incurs will be its (own) loss. ‘Our Lord! Do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes. Our Lord! Do not burden us as you burdened those before us. Our Lord! Do not burden us with more than we have the strength to bear. Excuse us, and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Master. So help us against the disbelieving people.’

sections.title: Sura Al-Imran (Sura No. 3 : Verses 1, 2, 18, 19 first part), Sura Al-Hadid (Sura No. 57 : Verses 1, 2, 3), Sura Al-Hashr (Sura No. 59 : Verses 20-24)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
|||
Sura Al-Imran (Sura No. 3 : Verse 1-2)::1. Alif, Lam, Mim.
2. Allah! There is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the All-Sustaining.
|||
Sura Al-Imran (Sura No. 3 : Verse 18, 19[FirstPart])::3. Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him. And (so do) the angels and those possessing knowledge. (He is) the Maintainer of Justice. There is no god but Him, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
4. Indeed, the (true) religion in Allah’s sight is Islam.
|||
Sura Al-Hadid (Sura No. 57 : Verse 1-3)::5. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
6. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
7. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. And He is All-Knowing of everything.
|||
Sura Al-Hashr (Sura No. 59: Verse 20-24)::6. The inmates of the Hellfire cannot be equal to the residents of Paradise. It is the residents of Paradise who will be victorious.
7. Had We sent this Qur’an down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled (to pieces and) torn asunder by the fear of Allah. We offer such illustrations for people, so perhaps they may reflect.
8. He is Allah, besides Whom there is no god, the Knower of the Unseen and the seen. He is the Most-Compassionate, the All-Merciful.
9. He is Allah, besides Whom there is no god: the All-Sovereign, the Most Holy, the All-Perfect, the Securer, the Guardian (watching all), the All-Mighty, the Most Supreme (and) the All-Magnanimous. Glorified is Allah from whatever they associate with Him (in worship).
10. He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator (and) the Shaper. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.

sections.title: Surah Al-Muzzammil (Surah No. 73)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. O you enfolded (in your cloak)!
2. Rise (to pray) in the night, but (for) a short while,
3. half of it or reduce it a little,
4. or add to it, and recite the Qur’an distinctly in a measured tone.
5. Indeed, We shall soon send you a substantial Word.
6. Indeed, the vigil of the night is more impactful in crushing (the lower self) and more suitable for (creating harmony between the heart and) speech.
7. Indeed, during the day, you are extensively engaged (in your affairs).
8. Remember the Name of your Lord and dedicate yourself to Him with complete dedication (detaching your heart from everything else).
9. (He is) the Lord of the East and the West. There is no god but Him, so take Him as (your) Guardian.
10. Remain patient over what they say, and keep away from them in a graceful manner.
11. Leave Me with the deniers—(the ones) living in luxury—and give them a little respite (so that their evil deeds may cross the limit).
12. Surely, We have heavy shackles (for them) and the Blazing Fire,
13. and choking food and a painful punishment,
14. on the Day when the earth and the mountains will shake violently, and the mountains will become heaps of shifting sand.
15. Indeed, We have sent a Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) to you as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.
16. Then Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, and We seized him with a terrible grip.
17. If you disbelieve, how will you guard yourselves against (the torment of) the Day that will turn children grey-headed,
18. (and) the heaven will split apart? His promise is bound to be fulfilled.
19. Surely, this (Qur’an) is a Reminder. So whoever wishes, let him take the path towards his Lord.
20. (O Prophet!) Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand nearly two-thirds of the night (in prayer), and (sometimes) half of it, and (sometimes) a third of it, and a group of those who are with you (also join you in the night vigil). Allah measures the night and the day. He knows that you (believers) cannot endure it. So He has turned to you (in mercy). Therefore, recite (in the prayer) whatever you can from the Qur’an easily. He knows that some of you will be sick while others will travel in the land, seeking Allah’s grace, yet others will fight in the way of Allah. So recite whatever of it is feasible (in the prayer). Establish the prayer, pay the alms due, and lend Allah a generous loan. Whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with Allah (in a form) that is better and greater in reward. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Most-Forgiving, All-Merciful.

sections.title: Surah Wadduha (Surah No. 93)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. By the morning brightness,* [* It may also refer to the raising of the Prophet Muhammad (blessings and peace be upon him), whose radiance replaced the darkness of ignorance with the light of guidance.]
2. by the night, when it calms and covers (the daylight with its darkness),* [* According to Qatada, Muqatil and Ja‘far al-Sadiq, ‘ al-duha ’ may also refer to the time when All-Mighty Allah spoke to Musa at Mount Sinai (al-Tur), whereas ‘ al-layl ’ may refer to the Night of Ascension ( al-Mi‘raj ) when All-Mighty Allah spoke to Prophet Muhammad (blessings and peace be upon him). See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi, al-Lubab and other authoritative books of tafsir .]
3. (O Prophet!) Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor is He displeased with you.
4. Surely, whatever moment (of your Prophetic period) comes after will be far better for you than the former. (Or: The exalted station of the next life will surely be far better for you than the one in this life).
5. And surely your Lord shall give you (so much) that you will be well pleased.
6. Did He not find you an orphan and sheltered you (with a graceful position)?* [* This verse can also mean: ‘Did He not find you (compassionate) and provide shelter to the orphans (through you)?’ See: al-Tha‘labi, al-Razi, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan, Abu Hafs al-Hanbali, al-Qadi ‘Iyad, al-Zurqani and others.]
7. He found you lost (in His love) and guided you (to your destination).* [* It may also mean: ‘He found you (as a guide) amongst an unguided people and guided them through you.’ Or: ‘He found your nation misguided and guided them through you.’ It can also mean: ‘He found you all alone, unrecognised among the people, and guided (them to you).’ Scholars have given another possible meaning to this verse: ‘He found you like a tree in a desert, which shows the way to lost people, so He guided them to the right path through you.’ Scholars have also offered another meaning: ‘He has found you in an overwhelming wish of the Qibla (the Ka‘ba of Mecca), and He will guide you (through His command) towards it.’ In this translation, ‘ al-dall ’ means ‘lover’ or ‘wisher’. al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, al-Farra’ and other great scholars of the pious predecessors have reported these meanings. See: al-Tha‘labi, al-Razi, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan, Abu Hafs al-Hanbali, al-Qadi ‘Iyad, al-Zurqani and others.]
8. He found you in need (of His support) and enriched you (with His abundant favours).* [* It can also mean: ‘He found you benevolent and (through you) fulfilled the needs of the poor.’ It may also mean: ‘He found you in need (of support for your Prophetic Mission) and strengthened you (through the support of Abu Talib, Khadija, Abu Bakr and others).’ It can also mean: ‘He found you in need (of Divine Proofs and Manifest Signs), and He made you self-sufficient (by bestowing these upon you).’ In verses 6, 7 and 8: ‘ yatiman ’ is considered the direct object of ‘ fa-’awa ’, ‘ dallan ’ the direct object of ‘ fa-hada ’ and ‘‘ a’ilan ’ the direct object of ‘ fa-aghna ’. See: al-Tha‘labi, al-Razi, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan, Abu Hafs al-Hanbali, al-Qadi ‘Iyad, al-Zurqani and others.]
9. So, as for the orphan, never oppress (him).
10. And as for the beggar, never repulse (him).
11. And as for your Lord’s blessing, proclaim (it well).

sections.title: Surah Ash-Sharh (Surah No. 94)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Have We not expanded your breast for you (Esteemed Prophet!),* [* This expansion may refer to the Divine light, knowledge and wisdom from Allah’s Presence, filling the breast of the Holy Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him).]
2. and relieved you of your burden,* [* This burden may refer to the resistance of the Meccan polytheists against the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him) and the persecution of his followers.]
3. that weighed heavily upon your back.
4. Did We not raise your remembrance for you (and exalted your name)?* [* It refers to making the Prophet’s remembrance everlasting, joining his name with Allah’s name in every commandment, and celebrating his praise in this world and the Hereafter.]
5. So, indeed, with (every) hardship comes ease.
6. Indeed, with (every) hardship comes ease.
7. So, once you have fulfilled (your duty), strive (in acts of devotion),
8. and turn to your Lord eagerly.

sections.title: Surah At-Takathur (Surah No. 102)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. The competition of wealth accumulation distracts you (from God),
2. until you visit the graves.
3. No, indeed! Soon you will come to know!
4. Again, no, indeed! Soon you will come to know!
5. No, indeed! If only you had known (the consequence of greed) with certain knowledge (you would have acted differently).
6. You will most definitely see the Hellfire.
7. Again, you will most surely see it with the eye of certainty.
8. Then, surely you will be questioned that Day, about the blessings (bestowed upon you in the world).

sections.title: Surah Al-Fil (Surah No. 105)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?
2. Did He not cause their scheme to end in confusion,
3. and sent upon them flocks of birds,
4. pelting them with stones of baked clay,
5. and made them (perish) like the straw chewed up?

sections.title: Surah Al-Kafirun (Surah No. 109)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Say: ‘O disbelievers!
2. I do not worship what you worship,
3. nor do you worship what I worship.
4. And I will never worship what you worship,
5. nor will you worship what I worship.
6. You have your religion, and I have my religion.’

sections.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas (Surah No. 112) - 3 times
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Say: ‘He is Allah, the Unique One.
2. Allah is Self-Sufficient and the Most Superior Sustainer upon whom all depend.
3. He neither begets nor was He begotten (i.e. He is neither a father nor a son).
4. And none is equal (or comparable) to Him.’

sections.title: Surah Al-Falaq (Surah No. 113)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Say: ‘I seek refuge in the Lord Who brought the universe into existence with an explosion (or: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak),
2. against the harm of whatever He has created,
3. and against the harm of the night when it becomes utterly dark,
4. and against the harm of those (witches) blowing on knots,
5. and against the harm of the envious when he envies.’

sections.title: Surah An-Nas (Surah No. 114)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. Say: ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind,
2. the Supreme Sovereign of humankind,
3. the God of humankind,
4. from the evil of the whisperings of the sneaky (Satan),
5. who whispers into the breasts of humans,
6. from among the jinn and humans.’

sections.title: Surah Al-Fateha (Surah No. 1)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
1. All praise be to Allah, the Lord of all worlds,
2. the Most Compassionate, the All-Merciful,
3. Master of the Day of Judgement.
4. (O Allah!) You alone we worship, and from You alone we seek help.
5. Guide us upon the straight path,
6. the path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray.

sections.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (Surah No. 2 : Verses 1-5), Surah An-Nisa (Surah No. 4 : Verse 80), Surah Al-Maidah (Surah No. 5 : Verse No. 15), Surah At-Taubah (Surah No. 9 : Verses No. 128, 129), Surah Al-Anbiya (Surah No. 21 : Verse No. 107), Surah Al-Ahzab (Surah No. 33 : Verses 40 & 56)
sections.text:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful
|||
Surah Al-Baqarah (Surah No. 2 : Verses 1-5)::1. Alif, Lam, Mim.
2. This is the (Glorious) Book. There is no doubt about it. It is a guide for those who are God-conscious,
3. who believe in the Unseen, establish prayer and spend from what we have provided them,
4. and who believe in what has been revealed to you (O Prophet) and what was revealed before you, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.
5. They are the ones upon guidance from their Lord, and they are the ones who shall be successful.
|||
Surah An-Nisa (Surah No. 4 : Verse 80)::6. Whoever obeys the Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) has indeed obeyed Allah. And whoever turns away (from you), We have not sent you to be a keeper over them.
|||
Surah Al-Maidah (Surah No. 5 : Verse 15)[Last Part]::7. There has indeed come to you a light from Allah (i.e. Prophet Muhammad (blessings and peace be upon him) and a Manifest Book (i.e. the Holy Qur’an).
|||
Surah At-Taubah (Surah No. 9 : Verse 128,129)::8. Indeed, a Messenger has come to you from among yourselves. Very stressful for him (blessings and peace be upon him) is your suffering. He is deeply concerned for your well-being and is most kind and merciful to the believers.
9. But if they turn away, say: ‘Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god except Him. In Him, I have put my trust. And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
|||
Surah Al-Anbiya (Surah No. 21 : Verse 107)::10. And (Esteemed Prophet,) We did not send you but as a mercy for all (creatures of) the worlds.
|||
Surah Al-Ahzab (Surah No. 33 : Verse 40)::11. Muhammad (blessings and peace be upon him) is not the father of any of your men. However, he is the Messenger of Allah and the Last of the Prophets. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
|||
Surah Al-Ahzab (Surah No. 33 : Verse 56)::12. Indeed, Allah and (all) His angels (continuously) invoke blessings upon the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him). O believers! You, too, invoke blessings upon him and salute him with worthy salutations of peace.

sections.title: Darood-e-Taj
sections.text:
1. O Allah, send blessings upon our Master Muhammad, the bearer of the Crown, the one honored with the Ascension (Mi'raj), the Buraq, and the Banner.
2. The remover of calamities, epidemics, famine, illness and suffering.
3. Whose blessed name is written, exalted, accepted for intercession, and inscribed upon the Preserved Tablet and the Pen.
4. Master of the Arabs and the non-Arabs.
5. His blessed body is sacred, fragrant, purified and radiant in the Sacred House and Sanctuary.
6. The sun of the morning, the full moon of the night, the highest in rank, the light of guidance, the refuge of creation and the lamp in darkness.
7. Beautiful in character, the intercessor for all nations.
8. The possessor of generosity and nobility.
9. And Allah is his Protector.
10. And Jibril is in his service.
11. And the Buraq was his mount.
12. The Mi'raj was his journey, and Sidrat al-Muntaha was his station.
13. "At a distance of two bow-lengths" was his desired nearness.
14. His desire was fulfilled, and his objective attained.
15. The Master of all the Messengers.
16. The Seal of the Prophets and the Intercessor of sinners.
17. The Companion of the lonely, the Mercy for all the worlds.
18. The comfort of those who love him.
19. The desire of those who long for him.
20. The sun of those who truly know Allah.
21. The lamp of those travelling the path to Allah and the light of those brought near to Him.
22. The lover of the poor, the strangers and the needy.
23. The Master of mankind and jinn, the Prophet of the Two Sacred Sanctuaries.
24. The Imam of the Two Qiblahs.
25. Our means of nearness in this world and the Hereafter.
26. The one honored with Qaba Qawsayn, the Beloved of the Lord of the Easts and the Wests.
27. The grandfather of Hasan and Husayn, our Master and the Master of mankind and jinn, Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Abdullah, a light from the Light of Allah. O those who long for the light of his beauty, behold the Light of Allah. He attained the highest rank through his perfection. He dispelled darkness through his beauty. Mawla Ali is the remover of difficulties. Hasan and Husayn are the beloved grandsons of Lady Fatimah. All his noble qualities are beautiful. That is Muhammad, the Chosen One ﷺ. Send blessings upon him, his family, his companions, and greet them with complete peace.

sections.title: Dua-e-Nur
sections.text:
1. O Allah, O Light! You are manifested through Light. Light is within Light. Yours is the Light, O Light.
2. O Allah, bless us and avert our afflictions. O Most Kind, we answer Your call; honor those who answer Your call. And on the Day when those in the graves are resurrected, grant us the best of this world and the Hereafter, together with nearness to You, sincerity, and steadfastness through Your grace. Send blessings upon the best of Your creation, Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions, and grant them abundant peace. O Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

sections.title: Darood-e-Tanjina
sections.text: 1. O Allah, send blessings upon our Master and Protector Muhammad and upon the family of our Master and Protector Muhammad, such blessings by which You save us from all fears and calamities, fulfill all our needs, purify us from all sins, raise us to the highest درجات (ranks), and enable us to attain the utmost goals of every خير (good) in this life and after death. Indeed, You have power over all things.

sections.title: Darood-e-Mahi
sections.text:
1. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the best of all creation, the noblest of mankind, and the intercessor for the nations on the Day of Gathering and Resurrection.
2. And send blessings upon our Master Muhammad and his family equal to the number of everything known to You.
3. And send blessings, peace and abundant grace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
4. And upon all the Prophets and Messengers.
5. And upon all the angels brought near to Allah.
6. And upon the righteous servants of Allah.
7. And grant abundant peace through Your mercy, Your bounty and Your generosity, O Most Generous of the generous.
8. By Your mercy, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy.
9. O Eternal One, O Everlasting One, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, O One, O Unique, O Absolute.
10. The One Who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. By Your mercy, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

sections.title: Darood-e-Khaas (3 times)
sections.text:
1. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad among the first generations.
2. And among the later generations.
3. And in the Highest Assembly until the Day of Judgement.
4. And at every time and every moment.
5. And in every gathering.
6. And in every place.
7. And upon his family.
8. And upon his companions.
9. And upon his wives.
10. And upon all of his descendants until the Day of Judgement.
11. And bless them.
12. And grant them peace.

sections.title: Swab e Takbir (3 Times)
sections.text:
1. Here I am, O Allah, here I am.
2. Here I am. You have no partner. Here I am.
3. Indeed, all praise, all blessings, and all sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.

sections.title: Surah As-Saffat (Surah No. 37 : Verses 180-182)
sections.text:
1. Glorified is your Lord, the Lord of Majesty, far above what they attribute to Him.
2. And peace be upon the Messengers.
3. And all praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.

sections.title: Du'a
sections.text: Read the Sijrah once and pray for your heart's desires.

sections.title: Salaam
sections.text: Send Salaam to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.)

sections.title: ADVICE OF HAJEE MAHBOOB KASSIM
sections.text:
Murids should read this Fateha in full, preferably in a gathering, as follows:
Every Thursday night after the night (Isha'a) prayer
Every Sunday evening after the evening (Maghrib) prayer
Every Holy Day / Night as per the annual calendar issued by Khanqah Qadriya Chishtiya Musharrafiya, 20 Royd Street, Kolkata - 700 016, India
